project_desc_1: I started this to find out how far I could get building with AI assistance. The original {link} had stopped being maintained, so there was something real to rebuild rather than a toy project. It has been running at my own feeder ever since.
project_desc_2: Frigate watches the feeder and flags anything that looks like a bird. YA-WAMF classifies it, checks it against BirdNET-Go audio, and stores the result. Every photo on this page came off that camera.

outbound.title: What leaves your network
outbound.intro: The outside services this install contacts, who makes each request and what it sends. Services at addresses you enter yourself, such as Frigate, your MQTT broker or BirdNET-Go, are not listed.
outbound.now_heading_unknown: Sending now, or depends on the owner’s settings
outbound.rest_heading: Off, or only when someone starts it
outbound.on_demand: When you connect, test or run diagnostics
outbound.inat_desc: Bird names and species details. Sends the species name.
outbound.inat_local_desc: Local seasonality in species details and regional model evaluation, when the feeder’s location is known. Sends the species and the feeder’s coordinates.
outbound.wikipedia_desc: Species descriptions. Sends the species name.
outbound.gbif_desc: Finds the range map for a species you open. Sends the species name.
outbound.weather_desc: Weather for each visit. Sends the feeder’s coordinates.
outbound.geolocate_desc: Finds a rough location when automatic location is on and no coordinates are saved. It sees this server’s public IP address.
outbound.places_desc: Names the place at the feeder’s coordinates in Settings. Sends the coordinates.
outbound.ebird_desc: Recent sightings near the feeder. Sends your API key and the feeder’s coordinates.
outbound.birdweather_desc: Reports each named visit to your station. Sends the species, the time, the confidence, your station token and the feeder’s coordinates when they are set.
outbound.inat_submit_desc: Observations you choose to submit. Sends the photo, species, time and location.
outbound.llm_desc: Behaviour notes, chart summaries and chat. Sends the photo or frames, the species, the time and weather, chart content, and your questions with the earlier conversation and analysis, to the provider you chose with your key.
outbound.notify_desc: Discord, Telegram, Pushover or email. Sends the species, confidence, time and camera name, links to the record and its media, the photo, and for email the weather, to the channels you set up.
outbound.garden_notify_desc: Alerts for Garden animals, which can use their own channels while every bird channel is off. Sends the animal, the time, the camera name and, if you chose it, the photo. With an instance address set, it also sends a link to the record, which contains that address, the camera name and the capture’s ID.
outbound.telemetry_desc: An installation ID, runtime details, and which integrations, notification channels and access options are switched on. Nothing about your visits.
outbound.telemetry_health_desc: A separate opt-in. Sends an installation ID, runtime and configuration details, and diagnostic events with addresses and secrets removed.
outbound.telemetry_forget_desc: Switching off the last telemetry opt-in sends one request asking the YA-WAMF telemetry service to delete this install’s history. Sends the installation ID, which is then replaced with a new one.
outbound.updates_desc: Asks the YA-WAMF update service for the latest release and reads one anonymous install count. Off with update checks.
outbound.downloads_desc: Fetches model files from GitHub, and from Google Storage for one wildlife model, when you download a model. A model evaluation fetches test photos from iNaturalist and Wikimedia, and a regional one sends the feeder’s coordinates to iNaturalist.
outbound.garden_model_desc: When an automatic Garden check is due and its model file is missing or damaged, the file is fetched from GitHub without anyone pressing a button. Sends nothing about this install.
outbound.model_repair_desc: At each start, an installed model that lacks its configuration file has it fetched from GitHub. Nothing is requested when none is missing.
outbound.fonts_desc: The app’s typefaces. Google sees the viewer’s IP address and browser.
outbound.photos_desc: Species photos load from Wikimedia and iNaturalist, which see the viewer’s IP address and the photo requested.
outbound.osm_desc: Maps of the feeder’s location, what eBird reports nearby, and ranges. OpenStreetMap sees the viewer’s IP address and the area shown.
outbound.gbif_tiles_desc: The range overlay in species details. GBIF sees the viewer’s IP address and the species.
outbound.oauth_browser_desc: Connecting Gmail, Outlook or iNaturalist opens that provider’s sign-in page in your browser.
outbound.oauth_server_desc: Once connected, this server exchanges and refreshes tokens with Google, Microsoft or iNaturalist, and reads the connected Google account’s email address.
outbound.tests_desc: Each test contacts its provider. Discord, Telegram and Pushover tests run even while the channel is switched off, with the credentials typed in the form or the saved ones, and carry the address of a placeholder picture at placehold.co, which Discord loads as an image. The email test uses the saved email settings only, needs email switched on, and sends no picture. The BirdWeather test uses the typed station token, or the saved one while BirdWeather is on. The AI test runs only while AI is on in the form or in the saved settings, with the typed or saved key.
outbound.diagnostics_desc: Asks Frigate, iNaturalist and the YA-WAMF telemetry host whether they answer, whether or not telemetry is on. Sends no data about this install.
outbound.guest_note: Shown for transparency. Only the owner can change these.
